title: Secure inference deployment criteria and rollforward playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Purpose: Define minimum security & compliance acceptance criteria for customer-facing private/VPC inference deployments and provide a rollforward (operational signoff + remediation) playbook. This ticket consolidates requirements across SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, and KMS/HSM integration into a single evidence-driven acceptance artifact to be used by field onboarding and engineering signoff teams.

Scope: Applies to Private and Dedicated Dedicated-with-VPC deployments where customers require enterprise controls (SAML federation, scoped operator roles, customer KMS/BYOK, tamper-evident audit trails). Does NOT change hosted API defaults.

Out of scope: deep HSM operator implementation details (owned by ENG), full legal contract changes (owned by Legal), and SOC/ISO audit artifacts generation. This work is the product-level acceptance gating + playbook for rollout/rollback decisions.
scope_changes: 2025-11-18: Added explicit requirement for SCIM provisioning support after field ask (PM request).
2025-11-25: Narrowed audit log retention recommendation from 5 years to configurable 12 months with extension option to 36 months (legal/ops trade-off).
2025-11-30: Removed mandatory hardware HSM for initial GA; HSM support remains required within 2 quarters as an optional add-on.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Customer can configure IdP metadata in the Console and validate SAML assertions in a tenant-specific test flow (successful sign-in, attribute mapping).
SCIM: Provisioning endpoints exist and can sync users & groups; mappings for 'role' attribute to Redwood RBAC are documented and validated in staging.

RBAC: Three baseline roles (Operator, Admin, Readonly) exist; custom role templates supported; actions are scoped to model routes and deployment groups. Unit tests + e2e test accounts verify permission boundaries.

Audit logs: All admin actions, auth events, and model-prediction ingestion metadata are written to append-only audit logs with cryptographic hash chaining for tamper-evidence. Retention and export APIs must be present.

KMS/BYOK: Customer-provided keys can be registered via the Console or API; key wrapping is implemented so that model artifacts and secret blobs are encrypted under customer keys. Rotation path documented and validated with a simulated key rollover.
HSM support: HSM-backed key stores are supported as an option; integration test demonstrates signing/unwrap operations using an HSM simulator (real HSM acceptance is part of later QA).
Operational tests: Onboarding smoke test verifies SSO sign-in, SCIM sync, a role-assigned user performing a deploy, and audit log entry creation. Automated test script is present in the ops repo.
Compliance evidence: A single evidence bundle (links to config screenshots, logs, test outputs, and key registration events) is generated for signoff.
signoff_checklist: PM acceptance: PRD updated to include final criteria and runbook.
Security engineering: Threat model reviewed and no open critical findings.
Platform engineering: Feature flags and rollout gating implemented; fail-open behavior assessed.
DevOps/Infra: Backup & rotation playbook validated; KMS integration tests pass in staging.
Legal/Compliance: Retention policy and export controls are acceptable for customer contracts.
Customer Success: Onboarding checklist validated with two pilot customers and feedback captured.
SRE: SLIs defined for auth latency and audit log write rate; alerting configured.
Documentation: Console UI documentation, API reference, and runbook published to the internal docs site.
Signatures required: [PM, Security Eng Lead, Platform Eng Lead, SRE Lead, Legal Representative]
notes:
Key trade-offs: we prioritize a pragmatic GA surface that supports BYOK via cloud KMS while deferring mandatory hardware HSM to avoid blocking customers. SCIM was added due to strong customer demand; this increases onboarding complexity but reduces long-term operator load. Audit tamper-evidence implemented with hash-chaining to reduce trust surface without requiring a third-party ledger for initial GA.

Open questions for the next review: should operator role include 'can-rotate-keys' by default? (Security recommends 'no' and explicit opt-in). How long should the default audit retention be for enterprise customers in EU regions where data residency is required?
